title: Hold several model projects side by side and switch between them

needs: An operator works on more than one model, and today every one of them writes into the same work directory: `manifests.root()` returns the installation directory and nothing overrides it.
Reports from unrelated models share one identity counter, so the first operation of a second model was allocated `009` instead of `001`.
The viewer merges unrelated models: every parentless report lands in one outliner group named after whichever model was scanned first, and the operation count in the top bar adds them together.
`prune --keep` applies its window across every report in the directory, so retention for one model is decided by activity on another.
Parent resolution matches an operation's input fingerprint against every report on disk, so two projects starting from the same source file can be linked to each other.
The operator needs to move between projects in the viewer rather than rebuilding a separate page and opening it by hand.
context: `root()` currently answers two different questions with one value: where the code lives (`tools/*.op.json`, `locales/`, `viewer/`, `logics/`) and where the work lives (`work/ops`, `work/in`, `work/renders`, `work/viewer`, `work/doctor.json`).

The job file handed to the engine carries a single `root`, which the Blender scripts use both to import `meshanvil_engine` and to locate `work/renders`; splitting the roots has to keep both resolvable.
Identity allocation is an exclusive-create race over the report directory, so scoping it to a project is a matter of which directory is scanned, not of adding a lock.
The viewer is a static local page over a generated data file and must stay read-only: switching project cannot start a process, fetch, or write.
The repository is itself a working project today. The demo chain and `tools/build_demo_chain.sh` run against the installation directory and must keep working untouched.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Code location and work location are resolved separately; manifests, locales, viewer sources and Logics documents come from the installation, while reports, sources, renders, the built page and the setup report come from the active project.
AC2: An operator can create and select a project without editing a file or exporting a variable in every shell, and the command line reports which project it resolved and from where.

AC3: Identity allocation, parent resolution by fingerprint, and prune retention are each scoped to the active project; the first operation of a new project is `001` and no report of one project can become the parent of another.
AC4: The viewer offers a project switcher listing the projects that hold reports, and selecting one shows that project's chain, counts and renders without a rebuild, a server, or any write.
AC5: The viewer names the active project everywhere it currently names a fixed path, and the operation count, branch count and totals describe that project alone.
AC6: An installation with no project marker keeps behaving exactly as it does today, `tools/build_demo_chain.sh` included, and an existing work directory is readable without a migration step.
AC7: A source file outside the active project is still accepted as an operation target, and the read-only refusal that protects the sources directory follows the active project.
AC8: Automated checks cover the split: a run in one project leaves another untouched, identities restart, and the browser smoke exercises the switcher and fails when it is absent.

product.title: Multi-project operator workspaces
product.overview: Lets one installation serve several model projects, each with its own reports, artefacts and viewer, and lets the operator move between them from the page instead of rebuilding it.
goals: Separate where the tool is installed from where a project's work is kept.
Make every per-project namespace -- identity, parentage, retention -- actually per project.
Let the operator see and switch projects from the viewer without leaving read-only.
Keep the current single-directory behaviour working with no migration.
non_goals: A project database, registry service, daemon or hosted workspace.
Comparing or merging chains across projects in one graph.
Moving or rewriting reports that already exist on disk.
Changing the report schema, operation behaviour or geometry results.
Remote or shared projects, locking between machines, or multi-user access control.

backlog_items.title: Split the code root from the work root
problem: `manifests.root()` is derived from the module file and is used for both the installed code and the operator's work.
Roughly fifteen call sites across manifests, runner, viewer, prune, doctor, i18n and logics_bridge mix the two meanings.
The job file passed to the engine carries one `root`, which the Blender scripts use to import `meshanvil_engine` and to place renders.
scope_in: Introduce a code root and a work root, and move every existing call site to whichever one it actually meant.
Carry both roots in the job file so an engine script can import the package and write renders to the right place.
Keep the work root defaulting to the code root when nothing else is resolved.
scope_out: Choosing or discovering the active project, which is a separate item.
Any change to report contents, paths already recorded in reports, or the schema.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Manifest discovery, locale loading, viewer source files and Logics document reads resolve against the installation and keep working when the work root is elsewhere.
AC2: Reports, sources, renders, the built page and the setup report resolve against the work root.
AC3: An engine script launched with a work root different from the installation imports `meshanvil_engine` and writes its renders under the work root.
AC4: With no project resolved, every path is identical to today's.

backlog_items.title: Resolve the active project without an invisible setting
problem: Nothing today depends on the working directory: the tool behaves the same wherever it is launched from.
An environment variable alone would make the destination of a run invisible, which is the failure mode this project exists to prevent.
The operator needs to create a project and know which one is active before running anything destructive.
scope_in: Resolve the project by walking up from the working directory for a marker, with an explicit override for non-interactive runs.
Add a command that creates the marker and the work directories for a new project.
Report the resolved project and how it was resolved in the setup check and on the command line.
scope_out: A registry of known projects stored outside the projects themselves.
Prompting, interactive selection or shell integration.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Running from inside a project directory resolves that project; running with no marker anywhere above resolves the installation, as today.
AC2: An explicit override selects a project for one invocation without depending on the working directory.
AC3: The setup check states which project is active and which rule resolved it, and the viewer's environment panel shows the same.
AC4: A target file outside the active project is accepted, and the sources directory that is refused as a write target is the active project's.

backlog_items.title: Scope identity, parentage and retention to one project
problem: Identity allocation scans the whole report directory, so a second model continued the first model's numbering and took `009` for its first operation.
Parent resolution matches an input fingerprint against every report on disk, so two projects opened from the same source file would be linked.
Prune applies its retention window across every report, so one model's activity decides another's artefact deletion.
scope_in: Scope the identity scan, the fingerprint search and the prune window to the active project's report directory.
Keep exclusive creation as the arbitration for identity so two runners in one project still cannot collide.
Leave already-written reports and their recorded paths untouched.
scope_out: Cross-project parentage, even when two projects share a source fingerprint.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The first operation of a project with no reports is `001`, whatever other projects contain.
AC2: No report in one project resolves as the parent of an operation in another, including when both start from the same source file.
AC3: Prune considers only the active project's reports and artefacts, and reports what it dropped for that project.
AC4: Two runners inside one project still cannot claim the same identity.

backlog_items.title: Add a project switcher to the viewer
problem: The viewer is built for one report directory and has no way to reach another.
The top bar names a fixed path rather than the project, and the status bar totals describe whatever the directory happens to hold.
Switching today means rebuilding the page and opening it again by hand.
scope_in: Generate the page with the projects that hold reports and let the operator select one from the page.
Show the active project where the fixed path is shown today, in the top bar and the status bar.
Keep counts, branch totals and vertex totals scoped to the shown project.
scope_out: Drawing two projects in one graph, or comparing operations across projects.
Any fetch, server, build step or write from the page.
Persisting the selection outside the viewer.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The page lists the projects that hold at least one report and marks which one is shown.
AC2: Selecting a project shows its chain, outliner groups, renders and totals without a rebuild and without a network request.
AC3: The top bar and status bar name the shown project instead of a fixed path.
AC4: With a single project the page reads as it does today, with no empty switcher furniture.
AC5: New visible labels are present in the i18n catalogue and report data stays escaped.

backlog_items.title: Prove the isolation and keep the current setup working
problem: Isolation that is not asserted will be lost the first time a path constant is touched.
The repository is itself a working project and its demo chain must survive the split.
The existing browser smoke would pass whether or not a switcher exists.
scope_in: Assert that a run in one project leaves another project's reports, renders and artefacts unchanged.
Assert that identities restart and that parentage does not cross projects.
Exercise the switcher in the browser smoke and fail when it is missing.
Keep `tools/build_demo_chain.sh` and the fixture check running against the installation with no argument change.
scope_out: A performance or scale benchmark over many projects.
New test dependencies when the existing self-check and smoke paths are enough.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: One self-check run creates two projects, runs in each, and fails if either one's reports, renders or artefacts changed because of the other.
AC2: The self-check asserts the first identity of a fresh project is `001` and that no parent link crosses projects.
AC3: The browser smoke fails when the project switcher is absent, and passes with one project without requiring a second.
AC4: The demo chain script and the fixture check run unchanged against the installation and still produce their current reports.
